title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
excerpt: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated…

ai.summary: AnyS1 is a framework that converts human-authored procedural skills into a lightweight System-1 model for autonomous LLM agents, reducing cost and latency by offloading simple decisions from a large System-2 model.
ai.why: Developers can use this approach to optimize agent workflows by identifying and automating low-complexity decision points with smaller, faster models.

title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
excerpt: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful…

ai.summary: The authors propose the Resolution Hypothesis, claiming that agent evolution stalls because noisy evaluations cannot reliably distinguish better artifacts, despite improved proposals.
ai.why: Suggests developers should focus on evaluation robustness when iterating AI agents.

title: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
excerpt: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. Translating these capabilities into reliable task execution, however, remains a challenge for existing post-training methods. Offline supervised fine-tuning provides dense supervision on expert trajectories, but its flow-matching action expert is trained only on noised demonstration actions and never on the intermediate states produced by its own sampler; task-specific adaptation can also compromise pretrained capabilities. On-policy reinforcement learning trains on the policy's own behavior, yet sparse task…

ai.summary: The paper introduces HINT-WAM, a hindsight‑informed training method for World Action Models that adds supervision on intermediate actions to improve robot manipulation task execution.
ai.why: It offers a way to boost data efficiency and reliability of robot policies for developers building manipulation systems.

title: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
excerpt: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to use an external Zoom-in tool for fine-grained visual search. Recent works employ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) with tool-specific designs to enable such capabilities. However, achieving logical reasoning alongside accurate and efficient tool use remains a significant challenge. To address this, we shift the focus away from increasing RL complexity and instead identify SFT data quality as a key bottleneck. We then propose LogT (short for Logically Think with Images), a fully automated SFT data engine that explicitly enforces logic-chain-guided reasoning. LogT generates an SFT dataset featuring…

ai.summary: LogT proposes a visual‑search system that lets vision‑language models reason logically while using a zoom‑in tool for fine‑grained search, emphasizing high‑quality supervised‑fine‑tuning data over complex RL.
ai.why: Provides a simpler path to accurate tool‑using VLMs that developers can adopt for image‑based retrieval tasks.

title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
excerpt: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. To address the evaluation gap, we introduce RoughCut-Bench, which covers two practical settings: (1) a visually driven setting over video cases, covering highlight detection and selection, source-video ordering, and adherence to user requirements when provided; and (2) a speech-driven setting over automatic speech recognition (ASR)…

title: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
excerpt:
Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly becoming a dominant paradigm for AI applications. Recently, there is a growing demand to deploy large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models locally on consumer PCs to balance data privacy, API costs, and inference efficiency. However, unlike datacenter servers with abundant DRAM, consumer devices are tightly constrained in both GPU VRAM and host RAM, forcing massive MoE weights to spill across VRAM, host RAM, and SSD. Under such spilling, we observe that existing systems fail to fully utilize this memory hierarchy, treating the tiers as independent caches and thrashing in inference.
We present TIDEWAY, a system for efficient inference of large…

ai.summary: The paper proposes Tideway, a phase‑aware tiered memory manager that dynamically moves Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) weights among GPU VRAM, host RAM, and SSD to enable MoE inference on consumer PCs with limited memory.
ai.why: It lets developers run larger MoE models locally, reducing reliance on cloud APIs and improving privacy.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
excerpt: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases…

ai.summary: PReMind‑Bench is a diagnostic benchmark that tests personalized vision‑language assistants on recognizing physical hazards and applying user‑specific context such as allergies or mobility constraints.
ai.why: It provides a standardized way to evaluate safety‑aware, personalized AI assistants.

title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
excerpt: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. We formulate this setting as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a task that jointly refines spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories. To this end, we propose a framework that decomposes prediction into spatial and temporal stages using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads…

ai.summary: PROLA introduces Principal‑Orthogonal Low‑rank Adaptation, a method for predictive spatiotemporal weather downscaling that refines both spatial and temporal resolution of coarse forecasts to produce high‑resolution weather fields.
ai.why: It offers a more efficient way to generate localized weather predictions, useful for applications like agriculture or disaster planning.

title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
excerpt: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results…

ai.summary: Piccolo is a family of multimodal decision models ranging from 0.8B to 27B parameters that co‑evolve with training data via recursive self‑improvement, with Piccolo‑27B topping the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard at 75.59.
ai.why: The open models provide strong decision‑making performance for text and visual tasks, useful for building AI agents.

title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
excerpt: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. ai.summary: Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD) lets a diffusion transformer generate final pixels directly via a linear head, removing the separate decoder stage and cutting inference cost.
ai.why: Developers can build diffusion models that are simpler and run faster at inference time.

title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
excerpt: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training. Contrastive supervised fine-tuning teaches when and how to respond, while reinforcement learning with Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA) combines trajectory-level and local advantages to refine decisions, responses, and silence across multi-turn interactions. title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
excerpt: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. A single prompt admits many valid images, yet parallel predictions must converge on a coherent whole. We therefore condition all positions on a shared random state to coordinate parallel predictions, so that each draw yields a different but coherent image. Since the model tends to ignore this…

ai.summary: Jeveration extends the decision‑making paradigm of System One models to image generation, using a frozen vision‑language model to produce high‑quality images in a single forward pass while preserving global consistency.
ai.why: It demonstrates a new, fast way to generate images that could be integrated into real‑time applications or low‑latency pipelines.

title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
excerpt: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. To address these gaps, we introduce Game2Player, a framework that co-develops game environments and players to collect diverse and verifiable gameplay experience at scale. ai.summary: Game2Player presents a framework that co‑develops game environments and AI players to collect large, verifiable gameplay datasets for training visual agents.

title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
excerpt: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. Such feedback can rank evaluated configurations, but gives little information for deciding why a configuration is slow or which architecture parameter should be changed next. This limitation is especially severe because prefill and decode workloads can be limited by different resources, including compute throughput and HBM bandwidth. We propose CriticNPU, a sample-efficient DSE framework built around an online-calibrated mechanistic critic for NPU architecture design. The critic uses explicit hardware limits to evaluate NPU configurations…

ai.summary: The authors propose mechanistic critics that provide detailed feedback beyond scalar latency/power metrics for NPU design‑space exploration of LLM inference hardware.
ai.why: This enables more targeted hardware optimizations, helping engineers design faster, more efficient NPUs.

title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
excerpt: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. ai.summary: StatePortal is an agent that synthesizes checkpoint artifacts to reach deep GUI states in interactive software, reducing repeated effort across code commits.

title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
excerpt: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. We present BLIP-Live, a framework unifying data, metrics, harness, and training around a shared formulation of proactivity as effective causal response decisions balancing the two competing objectives of responding vs silence. title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
excerpt: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K T alongside subsequent steps at zero extra serial calls. ai.why: Offers a potential optimization technique for improving inference speed in recurrent or looped LLM architectures.

title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
excerpt: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
excerpt: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. ai.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, allowing AI agents to discover and purchase x402-enabled products, APIs, and data. Payments are processed in USD directly on the developer's AWS bill, eliminating the need for stablecoin wallets or separate API keys.
